title: Install | google-services-mcps
description: Every way to install the Google services MCP servers: npx, a global npm install, a one-line installer, or a clone. Flags, scopes and what an install writes.

blocks.text: Every route runs the same installer, `gsm`. Only the way you start it differs. The installer needs Node.js 20 or newer; the product's `engines` field requires `>=20`. It needs no build and no `npm install`.
Routes

blocks.caption: How to start the installer
head: Route
Command
Needs
rows: the line for your shell, below

blocks.text: The old package name `@firedmosquito831/google-services-mcps` is deprecated. It is the same installer; use `google-services-mcps`. A global install gives the commands `google-services-mcps` and `gsm`.
The one-line installers

Each line downloads the repository into `google-services-mcps` in your home folder and runs `node gsm.mjs` there with your arguments. The download folder is replaced on each run, and logins are not affected.

blocks.label: PowerShell
blocks.text: & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FiredMosquito831/google-services-mcps/main/scripts/install.ps1"))) install --agent claude --plugin gmail

blocks.label: Command Prompt
blocks.text: curl -fsSL -o "%TEMP%\install-gsm.cmd" https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FiredMosquito831/google-services-mcps/main/scripts/install.cmd && "%TEMP%\install-gsm.cmd" install --agent claude --plugin gmail

blocks.label: Linux, macOS and WSL
blocks.text: curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FiredMosquito831/google-services-mcps/main/scripts/install.sh" | sh -s -- install --agent claude --plugin gmail
Flags or the menu

With all the flags given, or with no terminal, nothing is asked: the command runs as written, and a missing flag is a usage error with the valid values. In a terminal, `npx google-services-mcps` with no arguments opens a guided menu. It covers installing, uninstalling, signing in to a Google group, signing out, the install list, the sign-in status, the products, the APIs and methods, the scopes, the checks and the version. Each answer shows the exact command it will run, and the install previews it with `--dry-run`.

blocks.text: What an install does

items: **Checks the requirements** of the agents you chose: Claude Code (`claude`), Codex (`codex`), OpenCode (`opencode`), and git when the Claude Code marketplace comes from GitHub. A missing one stops the install before any file is written, and the message gives the command that installs it.

**Installs what is missing, if you ask** (`--install-missing`). npm installs Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. git is installed with winget on Windows and Homebrew on macOS; on Linux gsm shows the command instead, because git needs sudo.

**Claude Code:** declares the `google-services-mcps` marketplace in the same scope as the plugin, then runs `claude plugin install <product>@google-services-mcps --scope <scope>`. Claude Code writes its own settings files.
**Codex, OpenCode and Antigravity:** copies each product's server files to `~/.google-services-mcps/runtime/<product>/`, and writes one entry per server into the agent's config file.
**Records the install** in `~/.google-services-mcps/runtime/installs.json`, so `list` and `uninstall` know what gsm did. Logins and tokens are never touched.

blocks.text: For Claude Code, the marketplace is declared in the same scope as the plugin. A `project` install writes both `extraKnownMarketplaces` and `enabledPlugins` into the folder's `.claude/settings.json`, so a teammate who clones the project gets both. An install from a clone records the clone folder, which is a local path, so do not commit that file.
Plugin options

Every Claude Code plugin has four options. `--allow-writes` and `--confirmation` set the first two at install time. The plugins need Claude Code 2.1.271 or later, because their options offer fixed choices.

blocks.caption: The four plugin options
head: Option
What it does
Default
rows: lists the tools that create, change, delete or send. Off, only reads are listed
`all`, `google` or `curated`: which tools the server lists. It applies when the server starts again
the folder for tokens and the OAuth client. Empty means `~/.google-services-mcps`

blocks.text: `gadmin` adds `admin_subject` and `service_account_key_file`. `gads` adds `ads_developer_token` and `ads_login_customer_id`. Show the options with `claude plugin configure gmail@google-services-mcps`; change them by piping JSON to the same command with `--values-stdin`, or with `/plugin configure` in Claude Code.
Update
Claude Code does not update plugins from this marketplace on its own. After a new release, refresh the marketplace and update each plugin you use:

blocks.label: Update the plugins
blocks.text:
claude plugin marketplace update google-services-mcps
claude plugin update gmail@google-services-mcps

Run the second line once per plugin. The new version loads in the next session, or after `/reload-plugins`. For Codex, OpenCode and Antigravity, run the install again so the runtime copy is refreshed.
Check and remove

`claude plugin list` shows each plugin with its scope and status. `npx google-services-mcps list` shows every install gsm made. `npx google-services-mcps doctor --plugin gmail` checks the plugin folder and the credentials, and exits 1 when a check fails.
To remove one install, run `uninstall` with the same `--agent`, `--plugin`, `--scope` and `--path`. To remove every install gsm recorded, preview and then remove:

blocks.label: Remove every install
blocks.text:
npx google-services-mcps uninstall --all --dry-run
npx google-services-mcps uninstall --all --yes

Uninstall removes only gsm's own entries and leaves a backup of each changed config file. It never deletes the token directory. To remove logins, use `logout` for each group, then delete `~/.google-services-mcps` by hand.
